title: Add large-state push benchmark
description:
Baseline benchmark so the `gopush` optimisations below can be measured rather than asserted.

## What

Extend `go/bench_test.go` with a **synthetic** large-state fixture (generated in-test — velox must not vendor a production capture) and benchmark the full push cycle:

- `Marshal` (the `MarshalFunc` path in `sync.go`)
- `mergePatcher.patch` (unmarshal + `objectDiff`)
- the no-change case (byte-identical input) and the small-delta case (one leaf field changed)

## Mock target: match these dimensions

Taken from a representative production `/api/state` capture, which is the workload that exposed the problem. Generate data that hits roughly these numbers:

**Overall: 341,817 bytes (342 KB) marshaled.**

| dimension | value |
|---|---|
| total paths (nodes) | 12,189 |
| object nodes | 2,502 |
| array nodes | 449 |
| string leaves | 5,790 (188,786 B total) |
| number leaves | 2,814 |
| bool leaves | 594 |
| null leaves | 40 |
| max nesting depth | 10 |
| string leaf length | p50 9 B, p90 40 B, max 1,980 B |
| key name length | p50 8 B, max 63 B |

Top-level distribution — the point is that it is **lopsided**, one subtree dominates:

| key | bytes |
|---|---|
| `machines` | 277,156 |
| — `machines.local` | 141,003 |
| — `machines.cJI9lhUjtQ` | 85,132 |
| — `machines.A9jexBGFhT` | 50,983 |
| `tools` | 38,080 |
| `config` | 6,193 |
| `chrome` | 5,662 |
| ~13 other keys | < 2,500 each |

Within the largest machine: `projects` 74,586 B, `toolConfig` 38,080 B, `terminals` 8,888 B, `agents` 6,109 B, `mcp` 3,589 B, `processTree` 3,443 B, `capabilities` 2,422 B.

The lopsidedness is the whole point — task 4's win comes from ~99.9% of those bytes being identical between consecutive pushes.

## Also benchmark realistic delta sizes

Observed on the wire over a 20 s SSE tap of a live server: **min 19 B, median 215 B, max 335,856 B** (the max being the initial full snapshot). The steady-state case to optimise is "342 KB in, ~215 B out".

## Measured baseline (Go 1.26.5, arm64, 341,817-byte payload)

| op | ns/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| `json.Unmarshal` → `map[string]any` | 8,402,363 | 1,585,544 | 34,014 |
| unmarshal + `objectDiff` (no change) | 10,896,244 | 1,629,906 | 34,942 |
| `bytes.Equal` on the same payload | 16,075 | 0 | 0 |

Decode runs at only ~40 MB/s and allocates ~4.6x the payload size, so state size translates almost linearly into push cost.

## Why

In the profiled production workload, `velox.(*State).gopush` is 66.7% of process CPU and 67% of allocated bytes — 309.63 MB of the 460.95 MB the process allocates per 30 s.
